proposals.before: (Old History of the Five Dynasties, Biography of Cui Zuan: Gaozu ordered the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to restore the civil and military dances and to fix in detail the rites of the winter court assembly and the music sections.
proposals.after: (Ouyang's History [New History of the Five Dynasties], Biography of Cui Zhi: Gaozu ordered the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to restore the civil and military dances and to fix in detail the rites of the winter court assembly and the music sections.
proposals.reason: 歐陽史 is Ouyang Xiu's Xin Wudaishi (New History), not the Jiu Wudaishi; 崔棁 is Cui Zhi, not "Cui Zuan".

proposals.before: (Old History of the Five Dynasties, Biography of Cui Zuan: Gaozu ordered the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to restore the civil and military dances and to fix in detail the rites of the winter court assembly and the music sections.
proposals.after: (Ouyang's History, Biography of Cui Zhi: Gaozu ordered the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to restore the civil and military dances and to fix in detail the rites of the winter court assembly and the music sections.
proposals.reason: Matches the Chinese 歐陽史·崔棁傳; prior English wrongly says Old History and Zuan.

proposals.before: Since the chaos at the end of Tang, ritual and music institutions had long been lost. Zuan, together with Vice Censor-in-Chief Dou Zhengu, Vice Minister of Justice Lü Qi, Vice Minister of Rites Zhang Yun, and others, drafted regulations for them.
proposals.after: Since the chaos at the end of Tang, ritual and music institutions had long been lost. Zhi, together with Vice Censor-in-Chief Dou Zhengu, Vice Minister of Justice Lü Qi, Vice Minister of Rites Zhang Yun, and others, drafted regulations for them.
proposals.reason: English "Zuan" continues the mistransliteration of 棁 (Zhi).

proposals.before: Since the chaos at the end of Tang, ritual and music institutions had long been lost; Zuan together with Vice Censor-in-Chief Dou Zhengu, Vice Minister of Justice Lü Qi, Vice Minister of Rites Zhang Yun, and others drafted regulations for them.
proposals.after: Since the chaos at the end of Tang, ritual and music institutions had long been lost; Zhi together with Vice Censor-in-Chief Dou Zhengu, Vice Minister of Justice Lü Qi, Vice Minister of Rites Zhang Yun, and others drafted regulations for them.
proposals.reason: Align literal English subject with 棁 as Zhi.

proposals.before: When the rites were complete, Gaozu was greatly pleased and bestowed gold and silk on Zuan. All the ministers and onlookers praised and marveled at it.
proposals.after: When the rites were complete, Gaozu was greatly pleased and bestowed gold and silk on Zhi. All the ministers and onlookers praised and marveled at it.
proposals.reason: Recipient of the gift is 棁 (Zhi), not Zuan.

proposals.before: When the rites were complete, Gaozu was greatly pleased and bestowed gold and silk on Zuan; all the ministers and onlookers praised and marveled at it.
proposals.after: When the rites were complete, Gaozu was greatly pleased and bestowed gold and silk on Zhi; all the ministers and onlookers praised and marveled at it.

proposals.before: In the year when Han Gaozu received the Mandate, in the ninth month of autumn, Acting Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Zhang Zhao submitted a memorial requesting changes to the music names of the dynasty. Stated in summary:
proposals.after: In the year when Han Gaozu received the Mandate, in the ninth month of autumn, Acting Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Zhang Zhao submitted a memorial requesting changes to the music names of the dynasty. Its outline stated:
proposals.reason: Chinese 其略曰 introduces the memorial summary; "Stated in summary:" is awkward and the source uses a statement formula, not a dangling fragment.

decisions.after: (Ouyang's History [New History of the Five Dynasties], Biography of Cui Zhuo: Gaozu ordered the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to restore the civil and military dances and to fix in detail the rites of the winter court assembly and the music sections.
decisions.reason: 歐陽史 is Ouyang's New History, not the Old History, and 崔棁 is Cui Zhuo (棁 = zhuō). The proposal rightly rejects Old History and Zuan but wrongly substitutes Zhi.

decisions.after: (Ouyang's History, Biography of Cui Zhuo: Gaozu ordered the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to restore the civil and military dances and to fix in detail the rites of the winter court assembly and the music sections.
decisions.reason: Literal citation must read 歐陽史·崔棁傳 as Ouyang's History, Biography of Cui Zhuo; Zhi repeats the wrong reading of 棁.

decisions.after: Since the chaos at the end of Tang, ritual and music institutions had long been lost. Zhuo, together with Vice Censor-in-Chief Dou Zhengu, Vice Minister of Justice Lü Qi, Vice Minister of Rites Zhang Yun, and others, drafted regulations for them.
decisions.reason: Subject 棁 is Zhuo, not Zuan; the proposed Zhi is still a wrong romanization of the same character.

decisions.after: Since the chaos at the end of Tang, ritual and music institutions had long been lost; Zhuo together with Vice Censor-in-Chief Dou Zhengu, Vice Minister of Justice Lü Qi, Vice Minister of Rites Zhang Yun, and others drafted regulations for them.
decisions.reason: Literal subject 棁 must be Zhuo; replacing Zuan with Zhi does not restore the correct name.

decisions.after: When the rites were complete, Gaozu was greatly pleased and bestowed gold and silk on Zhuo. All the ministers and onlookers praised and marveled at it.
decisions.reason: Gift recipient 賜棁 is Zhuo; Zhi is not the reading of 棁.

decisions.after: When the rites were complete, Gaozu was greatly pleased and bestowed gold and silk on Zhuo; all the ministers and onlookers praised and marveled at it.
decisions.reason: Literal 賜棁 likewise requires Zhuo, not the proposed Zhi.
其略曰 is already rendered accurately enough as "Stated in summary:"; "Its outline stated:" is only a stylistic rephrase of the memorial-summary formula.

claimRevisions.reason: Revising r0001 restores 崔棁 as Cui Zhuo in the cited biography title, so the work-association English must match.
Revising r0003 shows the extracted English personal name Cui Zhi mismatched 棁; the person remains 崔棁, so the English value must be Cui Zhuo.
